name: Pip Parcel
coverage: An original campaign with remembered choices and three endings.

chapters.title: A letter with feet
chapters.text: The island post office has one working glider and a bag of letters addressed to houses that have drifted away. Pip finds a note from their missing mentor, Sela.

choices.label: Follow Sela’s unfinished delivery route
Repair the glider with mechanic Bo

chapters.title: Addresses at sea
chapters.text: A family waits on a pier that now points toward open water. Their letter contains a new address, written in a language Pip barely knows.

choices.label: Ask the harbour families to translate it
Spend the afternoon following its sketch

chapters.title: Bo’s bargain
chapters.text: Bo can rebuild the glider or lend Pip a slow sail-cart. The glider needs the post office’s last spare parts.

choices.label: Take the sail-cart and keep the spare parts
Rebuild the glider for a longer reach

chapters.title: The drifting map
chapters.text: Sela has been drawing a map of moving islands. A lighthouse keeper offers a permanent job if Pip turns the map into a regular delivery service.

choices.label: Build a shared route with the island crews
Keep one dependable route of my own

chapters.title: A fleet of odd boats
chapters.text: The crews bring a bathtub, a fishing skiff and a boat with a very ambitious umbrella. They need meeting points everyone can actually reach.

choices.label: Use the addresses I checked along the way
Run a smaller pilot route before expanding

chapters.title: The long way home
chapters.text: Pip’s route reaches one isolated village. Sela is there, recovering from a broken glider and teaching children to draw their own addresses.

choices.label: Invite Sela to help train new couriers
Make this village the end of my route

chapters.title: The first storm season
chapters.text: The map changes during the first great storm. The islanders ask whether Pip’s service will grow, stay small or become a travelling school.

choices.label: Launch the shared fleet
Keep a small, dependable postal route
Travel with Sela and teach new couriers

chapters.title: Every island gets an address
chapters.text: The crews use the checked meeting points to keep mail moving through the storm. Pip runs the harbour office; Sela teaches, and Bo finally labels the spare-parts cupboard.

choices.label: Keep the completed journal

chapters.title: The route people can count on
chapters.text: Pip serves fewer islands, but the promised boat arrives. The harbour crews keep their independent routes, and Sela’s map remains available to them all.

choices.label: Keep the completed journal

chapters.title: Postcards from everywhere
chapters.text: Pip and Sela leave the office to the next crew. They travel between islands teaching children how to send a letter home. Bo receives an alarming number of drawings of umbrellas.

choices.label: Keep the completed journal

name: Della Quirk
coverage: An original campaign with remembered choices and three endings.

chapters.title: Spin cycle at midnight
chapters.text: Della manages a lunar laundromat whose washing machines predict tomorrow’s lost socks. Station manager Mott wants the predictions before the night crew sees them.

choices.label: Share the predictions with the crew
Use them to negotiate a better repair budget

chapters.title: A forecast in lint
chapters.text: Technician Rune predicts a station-wide uniform shortage. The night workers want extra machines; the budget covers only one.

choices.label: Ask the shifts to agree a rotation
Rent one machine for urgent uniforms

chapters.title: The repair clause
chapters.text: Mott funds the repairs but wants a private forecast subscription. Rune points out that a forecast is useful only if someone can act on it.

choices.label: Keep crew warnings in the contract
Sell a limited forecast and fund repairs

chapters.title: The sock exchange
chapters.text: The station opens a market in predicted lost socks. Customers suddenly pay more for tomorrow’s sock than today’s. Della can run the market or walk away from it.

choices.label: Make the exchange a worker cooperative
Keep the laundromat outside the market

chapters.title: One vote, two socks
chapters.text: Workers disagree about buying another shop. Rune wants ownership; courier Vega wants a shorter shift rather than more business.

choices.label: Keep both proposals on the ballot
Try a smaller expansion for one season

chapters.title: A plain old washing machine
chapters.text: Without the market, Della’s shop needs ordinary customers. Vega offers a transport contract that leaves one evening free each week.

choices.label: Negotiate hours with the night crew
Take a smaller contract and fewer shifts

chapters.title: Tomorrow arrives
chapters.text: The machines finally predict a day with no lost socks. Mott calls it a crisis. Della has to decide what the shop should be when nobody needs a forecast.

choices.label: Let the crew own the future
Run an ordinary shop with fixed hours
Sell my share and take my first holiday

chapters.title: The night crew owns the keys
chapters.text: The workers elect Rune and Vega to run different shifts. Della keeps a small share and an actual weekend. The machines receive a union-approved lint allowance.

choices.label: Keep the completed journal

chapters.title: Clean clothes, predictable hours
chapters.text: The laundromat leaves the sock market behind. Its schedule is modest, its repair fund real, and Della no longer answers calls from tomorrow before breakfast.

choices.label: Keep the completed journal

chapters.title: Closed for moonlight
chapters.text: Della’s share funds a holiday across the station’s quiet side. Rune and Vega continue the shop. Della sends them a postcard wearing deliberately mismatched socks.

choices.label: Keep the completed journal

name: Kiri Kite
coverage: An original campaign with remembered choices and three endings.

chapters.title: The unlit lane
chapters.text: Kiri joins a city relay league whose runners carry lanterns through moving night markets. Captain Asa needs an anchor runner; rival Jun offers a place on a faster team.

choices.label: Practise with Asa’s neighbourhood team
Trial for Jun’s faster team

chapters.title: A handover in the crowd
chapters.text: Asa’s team knows the alleys but loses time handing over the lantern. New runner Emi is afraid of dropping it in public.

choices.label: Let Emi set the practice pace
Take the difficult handover myself

chapters.title: The fastest split
chapters.text: Jun’s team records the fastest trial. Their anchor is injured, and the coach offers Kiri that place before discussing the extra workload.

choices.label: Ask the team to share the added training
Accept the anchor role for this season

chapters.title: The route changes
chapters.text: Rain closes the usual bridge before the final. The alternate route crosses Kiri’s home market, where vendors need time to clear a lane.

choices.label: Plan the route with vendors and runners
Train for the official longer route

chapters.title: Lanterns in the stalls
chapters.text: Emi and Jun help mark the market turns. A stallholder asks for the race to pause briefly during the evening food delivery.

choices.label: Build the pause into the relay plan
Move our changeover outside the market

chapters.title: The uphill straight
chapters.text: The official route has a steep finish. Kiri can gain speed through hard training, but their team has only enough spare time for one more full practice.

choices.label: Use the practice to test everyone’s split
Focus on my own final section

chapters.title: One lantern left
chapters.text: The final reaches its last handover. Kiri sees a clean individual lane and a harder route that keeps the whole team together.

choices.label: Run the coordinated team finish
Commit to the individual anchor sprint
Finish safely and become a coach next season

chapters.title: A city carries the light
chapters.text: The handovers hold under pressure. The team wins the neighbourhood cup, and the vendors keep their cleared lane for future races. Kiri and Jun organize the next league together.

choices.label: Keep the completed journal

chapters.title: The name on the split board
chapters.text: Kiri earns a place among the city’s strongest anchors. The team’s overall finish is modest, but Emi completes her first clean handover and Jun offers another season.

choices.label: Keep the completed journal

chapters.title: The next first race
chapters.text: Kiri leaves the last lantern at the finish and takes a coaching role. Asa finds new runners; Emi now teaches the handover she once feared. The league continues without needing Kiri to win it.

choices.label: Keep the completed journal

name: Cass Ledger
coverage: An original campaign with remembered choices and three endings.

chapters.title: A charge after closing
chapters.text: Cass balances the accounts of a late-night cafe. A dead customer’s receipt shows a payment from a company that never visited. Investigator Ren asks for the books; owner Jo asks for time.

choices.label: Give Ren the dated records
Ask Jo to explain the payment first

chapters.title: Two versions of the same bill
chapters.text: Ren finds a second receipt with a different total. The cafe’s cashier, Sol, remembers who printed it but fears losing their job.

choices.label: Record Sol’s account privately with Ren
Check the printer log without involving Sol yet

chapters.title: Jo’s missing week
chapters.text: Jo admits borrowing to keep the cafe open. A lender used the business name for another payment. Jo has messages but no full agreement.

choices.label: Preserve the messages and involve Ren
Ask the lender for the missing agreement

chapters.title: The lender’s offer
chapters.text: The lender offers to clear Jo’s debt if Cass signs a corrected ledger. Ren has enough to investigate, but a public case could close the cafe.

choices.label: Keep the original books for the investigation
Seek a settlement without changing the books

chapters.title: The hearing date
chapters.text: Sol agrees to attend the hearing. Jo wants the cafe’s staff protected from claims they took part in the scheme.

choices.label: Separate each person’s role using the records
Ask for a smaller hearing focused on the lender

chapters.title: Terms in the daylight
chapters.text: The lender accepts repayment talks but refuses to identify the other company. Ren can continue independently if Cass shares the records already held.

choices.label: Give Ren the untouched copies
Keep the settlement limited to Jo’s debt

chapters.title: A signature at the bottom
chapters.text: Cass must decide what to put their name to: testimony, a narrow settlement, or an exit from the cafe’s accounts.

choices.label: Give the complete documented account
Sign the limited, recorded settlement
Hand over my records and leave the job

chapters.title: The books remain open
chapters.text: The hearing establishes the lender’s false entries. Jo keeps a smaller cafe under a monitored repayment plan. Sol’s evidence is recorded accurately; Cass works with a new client who wants clean books.

choices.label: Keep the completed journal

chapters.title: A cafe with a debt
chapters.text: The settlement keeps the doors open but does not answer every question. Ren’s investigation continues on its own evidence. Cass records the limits rather than declaring the whole case solved.

choices.label: Keep the completed journal

chapters.title: Another ledger
chapters.text: Cass leaves copies with the investigator and moves to a different employer. Jo and Sol retain their own choices. The last receipt becomes a reminder that a job can end without a person’s whole life ending.

choices.label: Keep the completed journal

name: Nico Moss
coverage: An original campaign with remembered choices and three endings.

chapters.title: Wednesday, twice
chapters.text: The town wakes to Wednesday with no memory of Tuesday. Archivist Nico finds a ticket for a concert nobody recalls. Baker Fen remembers making a cake for someone who never arrived.

choices.label: Collect the town’s scattered memories
Trace the unused concert ticket

chapters.title: Cake without a birthday
chapters.text: Fen’s order book names a visitor who appears in no town record. Two neighbours remember different versions of the same doorstep conversation.

choices.label: Keep both accounts and their differences
Follow the one with a clear address

chapters.title: The empty stage
chapters.text: Musician Vale finds their instruments arranged for a show that did not happen. The theatre clock contains a folded note in Nico’s handwriting.

choices.label: Ask Vale to help read the note
Take it back to the archive alone

chapters.title: A town’s bargain
chapters.text: The note records an old agreement: the town traded one day each year to keep its archive from burning. This Tuesday held more than anyone expected.

choices.label: Rebuild the lost day from people’s records
Negotiate a different archive bargain

chapters.title: Pieces of a day
chapters.text: The records contain a wedding, an argument and a visitor’s farewell. Some people want the day restored; others ask for their private moments to stay private.

choices.label: Let each person choose which record to share
Restore only the public events first

chapters.title: A smaller archive
chapters.text: Vale proposes saving fewer records so the town no longer owes a whole day. Fen wants recipes preserved; Nico cannot keep every box.

choices.label: Ask the town to choose what it keeps
Keep a small travelling collection

chapters.title: The next calendar
chapters.text: The archive clock asks for a final agreement. Nico can restore Tuesday, accept a smaller archive, or take the town’s stories on the road.

choices.label: Return the day through the shared records
Keep a smaller archive and all future days
Become the town’s travelling archivist

chapters.title: Tuesday comes home
chapters.text: The shared records return the missing day without making every private memory public. Fen delivers the cake, Vale plays the concert, and Nico dates the first page correctly.

choices.label: Keep the completed journal

chapters.title: No more borrowed days
chapters.text: The town preserves a smaller archive and gives up the yearly bargain. Some details of Tuesday remain uncertain. Nico keeps that uncertainty in the record instead of filling it with a guess.

choices.label: Keep the completed journal

chapters.title: Stories with a return address
chapters.text: Nico leaves with a small archive cart. Fen and Vale send new records from home, and Nico returns each year for a day the town now keeps for itself.

choices.label: Keep the completed journal

name: Ari Brake
coverage: An original campaign with remembered choices and three endings.

chapters.title: Last bus to the depot
chapters.text: Mechanic Ari learns the district bus depot will close after summer. Driver Mel wants a worker-owned route; Ari’s daughter Rue offers a workshop space in another town.

choices.label: Help Mel test a community route
Visit Rue and inspect the workshop

chapters.title: Seats nobody counts
chapters.text: The route looks empty at midday but carries carers and night workers at its edges. Mel cannot cover every shift without help.

choices.label: Ask riders which journeys they need
Run the busiest journeys for a trial month

chapters.title: A workshop with a spare chair
chapters.text: Rue’s workshop is small but ready. Its rent is manageable if Ari takes repair work immediately; joining Mel’s route would delay the move.

choices.label: Arrange a gradual handover with both of them
Reserve the workshop and finish the summer contract

chapters.title: The summer detour
chapters.text: Roadworks force the last scheduled bus through three villages. An old passenger, Dev, offers a garage if the route keeps reaching their village.

choices.label: Build a village partnership around the garage
Keep the depot plan small and temporary

chapters.title: Who holds the keys
chapters.text: The villages can share one bus, one garage and a repair budget. Mel wants regular hours; Rue can help with the books from a distance.

choices.label: Write shifts and ownership with everyone involved
Keep my role limited to repairs

chapters.title: A clean tool drawer
chapters.text: Ari sorts the depot tools for its final week. Mel has a new driving offer, and Dev still needs someone to maintain the village minibus.

choices.label: Connect Dev with Mel and a local repair team
Finish my handover and move to Rue’s workshop

chapters.title: The final scheduled stop
chapters.text: At the depot’s last stop, Ari chooses what comes next. A shared route needs people, the workshop needs a mechanic, and a long break is possible too.

choices.label: Open the community route together
Move to Rue’s workshop
Take a break and mentor the next mechanics

chapters.title: A route worth keeping
chapters.text: The village partnership runs a smaller service with real shifts and repair money. Mel drives, Rue keeps the books, and Ari no longer carries every problem alone.

choices.label: Keep the completed journal

chapters.title: The next workshop
chapters.text: Ari settles into Rue’s workshop. Mel’s new job and Dev’s minibus continue on their own terms. The closed depot becomes one chapter of Ari’s working life, not its final page.

choices.label: Keep the completed journal

chapters.title: Time between journeys
chapters.text: Ari takes a quieter year and returns as a part-time mentor. Younger mechanics learn in the village garage. Rue saves the spare chair for visits rather than emergencies.

choices.label: Keep the completed journal
